gaps.sentence: We haven't received ___ information about the delay.
gaps.explanation: 'Information' is uncountable, so 'much' is required in the negative sentence.

gaps.sentence: ___ students joined the trip this year than last.
___ of the two films has been shown on television.
gaps.explanation: 'Neither of the two films has ...' is correct for two items; 'none' is not used for two and 'both/all' need a plural verb.

gaps.sentence: I don't like ___ of these two paintings.
gaps.explanation: After 'don't like', 'either' is used: 'not ... either of them' means zero of the two; 'neither' would double the negative.

gaps.sentence: He made a ___ of money in property.
gaps.hint: the article 'a' is already in the sentence
gaps.explanation: 'A lot of money' is the fixed phrase; 'a lots of', 'a plenty of' and 'a deal of' do not exist.

gaps.sentence: There's ___ at the door — go and see who it is.
gaps.explanation: 'Somebody' is used in affirmative sentences for an unknown person; 'anybody' belongs to questions and negatives.

gaps.sentence: He had ___ money, so he couldn't even buy a bus ticket.
gaps.explanation: 'Had no money' states zero and explains the result; 'none' cannot stand directly before a noun.

gaps.sentence: I haven't got ___ cash on me — I'll pay by card.
gaps.explanation: 'Any' is the normal quantifier in negative sentences; 'haven't got no cash' would be a double negative.
